unit.title: Goals and limits: a model, linear programming in 2D

lesson.title: Whole numbers only
lesson.subtitle: Yes-or-no loads, quick rules and why rounding fails

video.title: Whole numbers only
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Mr Okafor — your science teacher (main character)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, talks to the student)

scenes.visual: Mr Okafor beside a small truck in the schoolyard; boxes and furniture piled next to it.
scenes.animation: Boxes pop up around the truck; a weight sign shows 1,000 kg.
scenes.narration: Our school is collecting supplies for a village school, and your class is loading the truck. It carries a thousand kilos. Solar panels, desks, books, a water filter, footballs, chalk and paper: what goes on?

scenes.visual: Title card with the Darsi mark and the Optimization track chip.
scenes.animation: Mark pops in; title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: whole numbers only, and why the best load is harder to find.

scenes.visual: Six load tiles with weight and points, the heaviest first.
scenes.animation: Tiles appear as they are named.
scenes.narration: Each load has a weight, and points for how much the village school needs it. Solar panels: six hundred kilos, forty-two points. Desks and books: five hundred kilos each, thirty-three and thirty-two points. The water filter, footballs and chalk are lighter, and worth less.

scenes.visual: A desk cut in half with a red cross; then a switch with 0 and 1 beside each load.
scenes.animation: The half-desk shakes and fades; switches flip.
scenes.narration: You can’t take half the desks. Each load is yes or no: on the truck, or not. Buses, beds and teachers are the same: they only come whole. That makes the best plan much harder to find than on the garden graph.

scenes.visual: The truck fills: solar panels, then the filter, then chalk; the counter reads 60.
scenes.animation: Loads slide onto the truck one after another.
scenes.narration: A quick rule: load the most points per hundred kilos first. Solar panels give seven points per hundred kilos, so they go first. Then the filter and the chalk still fit. Sixty points.

scenes.visual: Ms Salma looks at the loaded truck, eyebrow raised. Three answer cards drop in.
scenes.animation: Cards bounce in one by one.
scenes.narration: Quick check! The quick rule took the solar panels first. Does that promise the best load?

scenes.visual: Two trucks side by side: quick rule (60) and desks and books (65), the second glowing.
scenes.narration: No promise. Desks and books together weigh exactly a thousand kilos and score sixty-five. The solar panels used up space that two other loads fill better. With six loads there are only sixty-four possible loads, so you can check them all.

scenes.visual: A crowd of 64 at the school gate; buses of 30 seats; the division on a card.
scenes.animation: The crowd fills in; the division types out.
scenes.narration: Watch out for rounding too. Sixty-four people are going on a trip, and a bus seats thirty. Sixty-four divided by thirty is two point one three buses.

scenes.visual: A village school: pupils at a river with cups; the water filter tile glows.
scenes.animation: The filter tile moves to the front of the queue.
scenes.narration: And who decided the points? Maybe the village pupils drink river water, and the filter matters most. A rule like “the filter must go” changes the best load. Ask the people you’re helping.

scenes.visual: A phone with the lab: load tiles, the truck, two buttons and a size slider.
scenes.animation: A finger taps loads; then the buttons; then drags the slider.
scenes.narration: In the app, tap loads onto the truck yourself and try to beat the quick rule. Then press Pack greedily, and Show the best load. Change the truck’s size: does greedy still miss?

scenes.visual: Ms Salma at the gate with two buses and a crowd. Three answer cards appear.
scenes.narration: Your turn. Two point one three buses: we book two. What goes wrong?

scenes.visual: The answer card gets the check; four summary lines and a takeaway bar.
scenes.animation: Lines tick in; the takeaway slides up.
scenes.narration: Four people have no seat: rounding down broke a limit. Remember: some choices only come whole, or yes or no. A quick rule is fast, but not always best. And ask the people you’re helping what matters most.

scenes.visual: Six paper cards on a desk with weights and points; a pupil sorts them into a box drawn on paper.
scenes.animation: Cards move into the box; a total appears.
scenes.narration: Try it yourself: make six cards, each with a weight and points, and set a weight limit. Pack them with the quick rule, then try to beat it. Can you find the best load?

checkpoints.prompt: The quick rule took the solar panels first. Does that promise the best load?

options.text: Yes: best value first is always best
No: a first choice can block a better mix
Only if the truck is very big

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — the panels used space that desks and books fill better: 65 points against 60.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — taking the best value first can block a better mix. Desks and books score 65, more than the quick rule’s 60.

checkpoints.prompt: 2.13 buses: we book 2. What goes wrong?

options.text: We pay for 0.13 of a bus

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — 2 buses seat 60, so 4 of the 64 stay behind. Rounding down broke a limit.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — 2 buses seat only 60 of the 64 people. Rounding down broke a limit.
